title: How can a class show what everyone thinks?
description: A classroom with many hands raised, and two friends who each name a favourite game. Every child in the class has an answer too, and the answers pile up with no clear way to show them. The video ends on that open question.
teaching_notes: One idea: a class holds many answers, and how we collect and show them decides how clearly we can read them. Watch for children who think one friend's favourite is the favourite of the whole class.

source: A question about the whole class
video_script.why: The child feels the need to gather and show many answers before any method is taught.
video_script.substitution: none: the opener only raises the question of how to show what a whole class thinks
